question: Find the vector equation of the line passing through the points $A(1,2,-1)$ and $B(3,-1,5)$. Hence, check whether $C(5,-4,11)$ lies on the line.
explanation:
Step 1: Position vector of a point on the line
The position vector of $A(1,2,-1)$ is
$$\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Direction vector of the line
The vector from $A$ to $B$ is
$$\overrightarrow{AB}=(3-1)\hat{i}+(-1-2)\hat{j}+(5+1)\hat{k}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Vector equation
Therefore, the required line is
$$\vec{r}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}+\lambda(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}).$$
Step 4: Verification of point $C$
For $C(5,-4,11)$, comparison of the $x$-coordinate gives
$$1+2\lambda=5\Rightarrow \lambda=2.$$
For $\lambda=2$, the remaining coordinates are
$$2-3(2)=-4,\quad -1+6(2)=11.$$
Step 5: Final conclusion
Both coordinates agree with $C$. Hence, $C(5,-4,11)$ lies on the given line.

options.A: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i+3\hat j+6\hat k)$; $C$ does not lie on it
options.B: $\vec r=(\hat i-2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k)$; $C$ corresponds to $\lambda=2$
options.C: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i-3\hat j-6\hat k)$; $C$ corresponds to $\lambda=2$
options.D: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k)$; $C$ lies on it with $\lambda=2$
